correctness.rationale: Conditioning on two specified disjoint endpoint pairs leaves uniform matching of N=2n-4 vertices. Single-pair indicator expectation is 1/M, M=N-1; two disjoint pairs have joint expectation 1/(M(M-2)); overlapping different pairs cannot cooccur. For the two cut systems U,V, potential edge counts A=(a+b)(c+d), B=(a+c)(b+d), common pairs C=ad+bc and shared endpoint multiplicity Q give Cov=[M(M-1)C-MQ+2AB]/[M^2(M-2)]. Independent SymPy factorization verifies this numerator equals 2[(ad-bc)^2-ad(a+d-1)-bc(b+c-1)]. The noncrossing specialization is 2st(s-1)(t-1)/denominator >=0, crossing strict sign follows immediately. Exhausting positive four-part compositions for n4/n5 shows no positive, while (3,1,1,3) at n6 yields 36/245; (0,2,2,0) at n4 yields 8/9 when gaps may be empty. Independent full residual-matching enumeration confirmed balanced k=1,2 cases, explicit positive/negative witnesses and asymptotics. Universal n proof is indicator algebra, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The joint degree dependence of two prescribed chords is a natural local statistic of random circle graphs, not implied by one-chord degree marginals or global crossing totals. The four-gap law sharply separates impossible negative correlation for noncrossing marks from mixed signs for crossing marks, and exhibits bounded negative versus linearly increasing positive regimes. The exact finite-size threshold is a motivated geometry boundary.

final_claim: For two prescribed chords in uniform random perfect matching on 2n cyclic endpoints, the conditional crossing-degree covariance has an explicit four-cell rational formula and complete geometric sign law, with sharp first all-positive-gap positive case at n=6.
limitations: Uniform matching conditioned on two prescribed chords, integer n>=4, empty four-cells allowed.
A covariance sign does not establish a full stochastic dependence order.
